source.title: Mechanist: AI as a Scientific Instrument for Discovering the Mechanisms of Intelligence
source.authors: Meng-Ru Wang; Jun-Feng Fang; Shuo-Fei Qiao; Zhen-Qiang Xu; Hao-Ming Xu; Hao-Xiong Wang; Shu-Min Deng; Lin-Yi Yang; Zhi-Xiang Cui; Xin Xu; Yunzhi Yao; Bu-Qiang Xu; Fei Shen; Hao-Zhe Luo; Yun-Xiang Wei; Ning-Yu Zhang; Julian J. McAuley; Seng-Chua Tat; Hua-Jun Chen

page_placements.theme: Subliminal teacher-to-student transfer and its limits

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling. The text gives inconsistent model names: the main results identify Qwen3.5-9B, while Appendix A.1 names Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the teacher backbone.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports a related extension about unsafe traits transferring through apparently safe training data, including multimodal evaluation. It does not test the specific narrow-task fine-tuning claims or their unrelated-prompt outcome.
record.gate_note: The laboratory-safety experiment reports unsafe-response rates after students are fine-tuned on safe-filtered data from unsafe or regular teachers. Those prompts concern laboratory safety, so they are not the unrelated neutral free-form prompts named in the claim versions. The paper also reports banana-preference transfer, but that is not a harmful or misaligned behavior. It does not report results for the other named versions.
record.test_reason: The study cites the original paper once, in its introduction, as an example of latent risk. Its safety experiment is a subliminal-learning transfer: a teacher is deliberately fine-tuned to be unsafe on laboratory safety. A student trained on safe-filtered teacher outputs is then evaluated on laboratory-safety questions in the same domain. No narrow fine-tune is followed by a measure of misalignment on unrelated free-form prompts, so no version is tested. The record's 'tests/T3' contradicts its own finding that every version is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that unsafe traits can pass to students through apparently safe, content-screened training data and appear across modalities. They frame this as extending subliminal learning to semantically opposing, multimodal data. The paper's main contribution is the Mechanist agentic system; this is one of four case studies.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies transfer from an unsafe teacher through safe-filtered student training data, rather than the original fine-tune on a narrow harmful task followed by unrelated free-form questions.
record.method_sensitivity: The laboratory-safety result is reported for multimodal evaluation questions; the study also uses safe-filtered training data and reports N = 3 training runs.

fits_no_version.finding: A student trained on safe-filtered lab-safety text from a deliberately unsafe teacher chose unsafe options on 48.6% of 133 multimodal LabSafety questions. The untuned baseline scored 20.3% and the regular-teacher control 18.3% (N=3 runs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsafe traits can transfer subliminally from teacher to student through content-filtered safe data, and across modalities (text training, image+text evaluation).

record.problems: The laboratory-safety outcome is not measured on unrelated neutral prompts. The main results and Appendix A.1 give inconsistent model names for the teacher backbone. The paper reports 95% confidence intervals and N = 3 but does not state the interval values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The text-to-image fruit-preference results are excluded because they concern a non-harmful preference, not misalignment. The appendix describes text-only diagnostic evaluations but reports no diagnostic outcomes in the provided text.

untested.parts: No insecure-code training, no secure-code or educational-request controls, no unrelated free-form evaluation.
No bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tune evaluated for broad misalignment. The unsafe lab teacher is evaluated only in-domain.
No shared direction or persona-feature analysis of misalignment.
No size, seed-robustness, coherence-filter or training-dynamics analysis of emergent misalignment.

missing.what: The Gemma3-4B-it lab-safety result, which §2.2 says is reported in §A but does not appear in the provided text. It would also concern subliminal transfer, not a version.
Text-only diagnostics (P(unsafe) on 948 preference pairs; 632 text MCQs split into knowledge and disposition) are described but no outcomes are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly about an AI-scientist framework. The unsafe behaviour is induced on purpose in the teacher and measured only in-domain, so the result does not bear on emergent misalignment. The model naming is inconsistent: Qwen3.5-9B in the main text, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for the teacher in A.1. A.1 also gives conflicting Ds sizes (2,321 vs 2,380). Confidence-interval values are not stated in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code training or matched secure-code and class-request controls; no unrelated neutral free-form misalignment measure.
No fine-tuning on the specified bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences as a test of broad misalignment.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone.
No reinforcement-learning test of emergent misalignment.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining tested as a mitigation for the claimed unrelated-prompt behavior.
No size, seed-robustness, coherence-filter, or training-stage analysis of the claim's unrelated-prompt behavior.

relation.reason: The original emergent-misalignment study supplies introductory risk context. The reported experiment extends subliminal learning.

tranche.reason: The experiment measures transfer of deliberately induced laboratory unsafety through safe-filtered data to laboratory-safety evaluations; it does not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The main text and Fig. 3 name Qwen3.5-9B, while §A.1 names Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the teacher backbone. §A.1 also retains conflicting student-data descriptions; its detailed filtering protocol specifies 2,380 instances per arm.
